h1: An immersion heater trips the electrics
title: An immersion heater trips the electrics | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand an immersion heater trips the electrics. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: Repeated protective-device operation needs electrical investigation. Do not repeatedly reset it to force a suspect immersion heater to work.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: A trip can relate to the heater, wiring, moisture or another circuit condition. G3 cylinder competence alone is not a diagnosis or proof of all electrical authorisation. The correct person must assess the electrical fault and related appliance safety.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Note what was switched on immediately before the trip and whether leaking water is present. Do not remove covers, bypass protection or attempt live measurements.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: Is repeatedly resetting an RCD an acceptable way to keep an immersion running?
faqs.answer: No. Repeated tripping can signal an electrical fault; stop using the affected appliance and arrange competent electrical assessment.
